pending_commit.commit_message: UPSTREAM: ec/chromeec: Fix battery ACPI mutex level Commit 07fe618 [chromeec: Add support for reading second battery info] added a mutex as part of the ACPI code to determine battery statuses. Windows is extremely picky about ACPI code, and attempting to acquire a level 1 mutex without first having acquired a level 0 mutex causes Windows to hang on boot. Since there's no reason to use a level 1 mutex here, change it to level 0. Test: Boot Windows on device with ChromeEC without hanging BUG=none BRANCH=none TEST=none Change-Id: I2525e57c6e46e0bdc446b3ad5c2e1b99eba0ea49 Signed-off-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@google.com> Original-Commit-Id: 047b23fc31e069c0cb372748e980da194ad59b95 Original-Change-Id: Icfb0817cfe0c49eb4527a12b507362939a6d32c6 Original-Signed-off-by: Matt DeVillier <matt.devillier@gmail.com> Original-Reviewed-on: https://review.coreboot.org/23697 Original-Tested-by: build bot (Jenkins) <no-reply@coreboot.org> Original-Reviewed-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@chromium.org> Original-Reviewed-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@google.com> Original-Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org> Original-Reviewed-by: Paul Menzel <paulepanter@users.sourceforge.net> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/916182 Commit-Ready: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Tested-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: soc/amd/common: Add S3 supporting functions Add functions that the wrapper will call to get and save the S3 data. The wrapper requires two types of data saved: * Non-volatile: Information that is the minimum required for bringing the DRAM controller back online. This change uses the common mrc_cache driver to manage the storage * Volatile: May be stored in DRAM; information required to complete the system restoration process. UPSTREAM: soc/amd/common: Replace missing AmdReleaseStruct() calls The AGESA spec states that "Failure to release a structure can cause undesired outcomes." Uncomment the one in AmdInitLate(). The function only dealocates the structure used for the AGESA entry point, and not the internal data used by coreboot. Release the structure in AmdInitEnv(). This appears to have been an omission years ago when duplicating agesawrapper.c for every mainboard was still common. run_oci: Allow 'run_oci destroy' to continue when the container doesn't exist session_manager kills 'run_oci start' process when the process (for starting ARC) does not return in 10 seconds. However, when session_manager does that, run_oci may die without cleaning up the container directory in /run/containers. This CL allows session_manager to call 'run_oci destroy' after killing off 'run_oci start' process to ensure that the container directory is always removed. power: powerd_suspend: Issue hcitool command only on Intel BT platforms Apparently, the Marvell bluetooth controller *sometimes* fails to respond to the command used to enable / disable mode change HCI event. The issue is rarely reproduced at random. So: * Issue the command only on platforms that have Intel BT controllers. * Timeout hcitool command at 2 seconds in order to ensure that a bad controller cannot take forever to respond. The timeout of 2 secs is taken from HCI_CMD_TIMEOUT in kernel. BUG=chromium:803272 TEST=Suspend / resume on Kevin does not issue the hcitool command. Suspend resume on a Soraka issues the hcitool command. Faking a hang (using sleep command instead of hcitool) kills the command and logs a message) Change-Id: I399f2ca794e135b703cbc0d46d15039649e30ab4 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/908249 Commit-Ready: Rajat Jain <rajatja@chromium.org> Tested-by: Rajat Jain <rajatja@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org>

gob_util: print more sensible GOB error message When FetchUrl reports GOB errors, it just prints raw HTML message received from the server, burying GOB's recommendations for the user on the ways to rectify the problem. This patch adds a parser which retrieves the contents of the <div id='af-error-container'> segment of the message. If the segment is present, the raw HTML GOB output is logged with a lower visibility, and the contents of the <div> segment is logged as warning. BUG=none TEST=verified that lib/gob_util_unittest succeeds running 'gerrit -g chrome-internal mine' when server access is not provisioned properly generates an error message, for instance: 14:14:59: WARNING: GOB Error: 401. That's an error. The requested URL was not found on this server. That's all we know.
